title: Cochain unit and counit for simultaneous derived scalar extension
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $B_1\leftarrow B_2\leftarrow\cdots$ a sequence of sheaves of commutative rings, and $A$ a sheaf of commutative rings with compatible homomorphisms $A\to B_n$. Let $\mathscr S(B)$ be the category of strict semilinear module systems, identified with modules over $B$ on the sequence site $\mathcal T=\mathcal C\times\mathbf N_{\ge1}$, with componentwise exactness [lem-pur-system-ringed-sequence-site]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories and write $[K]$ for the derived object of a complex and $[f]$ for the class of a chain map [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $p:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal T),B)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),A)$ have constant inverse image and the displayed structural maps, and use the canonical adjunction $\mathcal R=Lp^*\dashv Rp_*$, with unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$, normalized by the ordinary tensor/limit Hom correspondence [lem-coef-sequence-projection-derived-adjunction]. Write $U_0$ for termwise scalar restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], so $p_*I=\lim U_0I$. For every $n$, derived scalar extension $T_n=-\otimes_A^LB_n$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] is left adjoint to exact restriction $\operatorname{Res}_n$. Under its canonical K-flat comparison, the adjunct of a chain map $f:Q\otimes_A B_n\to K$ is represented by $x\mapsto f(x\otimes1)$ for every flat-term K-flat $A$-complex $Q$ and arbitrary $B_n$-complex $K$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].
For such a $Q$, put $M=(Q\otimes_A B_n)_n$. For every K-injective system resolution $a:M\to I$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex], the unit $\eta_{[Q]}$, in the model $Rp_*M=[\lim U_0I]$, is the class of the chain map
$$Q\longrightarrow\lim U_0I,\qquad x\longmapsto(a_n(x\otimes1))_n.$$
For every K-injective system complex $I$ and every flat-term K-flat resolution $q:Q\to p_*I$, the counit $\varepsilon_{[I]}$, in the model $\mathcal R Rp_*[I]=[(Q\otimes_A B_n)_n]$, is represented by the strict system chain map whose components are
$$Q\otimes_A B_n\longrightarrow I_n,\qquad x\otimes b\longmapsto b\operatorname{pr}_n^{U_0I}(q(x)).$$
All formulas use the canonical resolution identifications and are natural as derived morphisms, independently of the chosen resolutions. No K-injectivity of $U_0I$ or $I_n$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0FPI (lemma-adjoints-push-pull-compatibility), K-flat/K-injective representative counit; agent specializes the canonical module adjunction to the sequence-site projection and also records its unit and level scalar transposes.

proof.text: Apply the existing normalized sequence projection adjunction and retain all its ordinary presentations, derived universal properties, K-flat comparisons, K-injective comparison and normalized Hom identity. For a system chain map a, choose its ordinary cochain transpose h. Apply the ordinary inverse-transpose section formula in each degree with scalar 1 and cancel the inverse Hom equivalence. The resulting equation gives pi_n(h(x)) = a_n(1 tensor x). The normalized derived Hom identity is exactly the asserted unit equation, by the adjunction formula homEquiv(f) = unit followed by R(f).

For q:Q to FI, choose the inverse ordinary cochain transpose v. The ordinary inverse-transpose section formula degree by degree gives v_n(b tensor x) = b pi_n(q(x)). Apply the normalized derived Hom identity to v and cancel the ordinary Hom equivalence. Applying the inverse derived Hom equivalence gives L([q] followed by eta_I) followed by the counit = epsilon_Q followed by [v]. This uses only the already specified comparisons and no injectivity assertion for an individual level.

At level n apply the existing derived coefficient adjunction, which also supplies exact restriction and the normalized ordinary adjunction for s.E. The derived change-of-rings theorem supplies a pointwise homotopy-category universal pair LF, epsilon_h; its ordinary functor equals s.E because their prescribed object and map equations agree. Precompose its pointwise right Kan extension with the full essentially surjective homotopy quotient and transport through the quotient/localization factorization isomorphisms. This gives a cochain universal pair LF, beta. Uniqueness of the left derived functor gives c:LF isomorphic to s.T with c followed by s.epsilon = beta. Transport the derived coefficient adjunction along c. The coefficient theorem gives the normalized derived unit on a K-flat Q. The quotient unit equation and the compatibility of exact restriction with the two localization factorizations give its cochain version. Compose with restriction of [f] and use naturality of mapDerivedCategoryFactors to obtain the asserted Hom identity for arbitrary target K. Finally, apply the ordinary coefficient adjunction section formula in every degree; the image of 1 tensor x is tensorSection at 1 because scalar multiplication by 1 is the identity. Invertibility of s.epsilon on Q is the existing model field s.computes.

It has no repair note of its own, so the re-split rules do not apply; this is its ordinary first split with 6 steps, 4810 characters and no new nodes. Statement, stmt_deps, blueprint, source and created are unchanged from the base; no SGA citation; all three kinds of Mathlib search are present. Steps: (1) The scalar adjunct of [f]c equals [x↦f(x⊗1)] by the unit and adjunct clauses of lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction, with an arbitrary target. (2) I checked every cone, semilinear-strictness (ρ), differential and inverse identity by hand. (3) Φ([v]c_Q)=β_J[h_v] is what lem-coef-sequence-projection-derived-adjunction says for chain maps, and β_J=id for K-injective J; the declared tool use of lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition, for the K-injective direct-image convention only, is accepted as generic. (4) Unit: Φ(j)=Rp*(j)η with j=[a]c_Q, and Rp*(j) is the named model identification. (5) Counit: first-variable naturality gives Φ([v_q]c_Q(Lp*k)^{-1})=1, which matches the proof of Stacks 0FPI (sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-adjoints-push-pull-compatibility). (6) Independence of choices holds and no K-injectivity of U_0I or I_n is used. Small cases tested: Z→Z/2^n over a point (unit Z→Z_2), constant towers, a non-flat A→B_n, zero complexes. Candidates checked and ruled out as duplicates: lem-pur-sequence-adjoint-resolution-shifts (W_proet, specific), lem-sf-sequence-tensor-augmentation-unit, lem-coef-restricted-tower-resolution-acyclicity. The parent's steps 3 and 4 use exactly the clauses proved here. Route: the item's unit sk-prop-sf-biduality-general uses sk-def-sf-operations.
